questions.question: In a group of 200 members, 45% are teenagers and the remaining are adults. The average weight of the whole group is 62 kg. If the average weight of teenagers is 56 kg, then the nearest integral value of the average weight of adults is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total members = 200

Teenagers = 45% of 200 = 90

Adults = 200 - 90 = 110

Average weight (total) = 62 kg

Average weight of teenagers = 56 kg

**Formula used:**

Total weight = Average × Number

Total weight = Teenagers' weight + Adults' weight

**Calculations:**

Total weight = 200 × 62 = 12400 kg

Teenagers' total weight = 90 × 56 = 5040 kg

Adults' total weight = 12400 - 5040 = 7360 kg

Average weight of adults = 7360 ÷ 110 ≈ 66.91

**∴ Average weight of adults = 67 kg**

questions.question: The HCF of 21 and 49 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 21 and 49

**Formula Used:**

HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the largest number that divides two or more numbers exactly.

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Prime factorization of 21 = 3 × 7

Step 2: Prime factorization of 49 = 7 × 7

Step 3: Common prime factor = 7

⇒ HCF = 7

**The HCF of 21 and 49 is 7.**

questions.question: The difference between the selling prices with 19% profit and 11% loss is Rs.454.50. What is the cost price of the item?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in percentage = Profit % − (−Loss %) = 19% + 11% = 30%

Given that 30% of Cost Price = Rs. 454.50

⇒ 1% of Cost Price = 454.50 ÷ 30 = 15.15

⇒ 100% of Cost Price = 15.15 × 100 = 1515

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit = 19%

Loss = 11%

Difference between Selling Prices = Rs. 454.50

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/254765f321fda04698d9d7ff3629cd2d3c09bb2b560159217c5a4e51bae5bca1.png] 

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the item be x.

Selling Price at 19% profit (SP₁) = x + 19% of x = 1.19x

Selling Price at 11% loss (SP₂) = x − 11% of x = 0.89x

According to the question, the difference in selling prices is Rs. 454.50:

⇒ SP₁ − SP₂ = 454.50

⇒ 1.19x − 0.89x = 454.50

⇒ 0.30x = 454.50

⇒ x = 454.50 ÷ 0.30

⇒ x = 1515

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.1515.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

CP is the price at which goods are bought. SP is the price at which goods are sold. Profit occurs when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when SP < CP.

Effective Change in Profit/Loss

When moving from a loss percentage to a profit percentage on the same base, the total change in percentage terms is the sum of both values (Profit % + Loss %).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The fundamental relation between CP and MP is: MP × (100 − Discount %) = CP × (100 + Profit %).

questions.question: A person spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 15% and expenditure decreases by 10%, then what percentage increase will occur in his savings?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial income = 100 (assumed for simplicity).

Initial expenditure = 75% of income = 75.

Initial savings = Income - Expenditure = 100 - 75 = 25.

Income increase = 15%.

Expenditure decrease = 10%.

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income - Expenditure

Percentage increase in savings = ((New Savings - Initial Savings) / Initial Savings) × 100

**Calculation:**

New income = Initial income × (1 + 15/100)

New income = 100 × 1.15

New income = 115

New expenditure = Initial expenditure × (1 - 10/100)

New expenditure = 75 × 0.90

New expenditure = 67.5

New savings = New income - New expenditure

New savings = 115 - 67.5

New savings = 47.5

Percentage increase in savings = ((47.5 - 25) / 25) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (22.5 / 25) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = 0.9 × 100

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = 90%

**The percentage increase in savings is 90%.**

questions.question: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 40 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of diameter 0.8 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, three-fifths of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
questions.solution:

Diameter of hollow hemisphere = 40 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 20 cm

Diameter of 1 lead shot = 0.8 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 0.4 cm

Water overflow = 3/5 of hemisphere volume

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2)/(3) pi R³

Volume of sphere = (4)/(3) pi r³

Number of lead shots = Volume of water overflow ÷ Volume of 1 shot

**Calculations:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × 20³ = (2/3) × π × 8000 = 16000π/3

Water overflow = (3/5) × 16000π/3 = 3200π

Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × 0.4³ = (4/3) × π × 0.064 

Number of lead shots = 3200π ÷ [(4/3) × π × 0.064] = 37500

**∴ Number of lead shots = 37500**

⇒ Increase = ₹3.55

questions.question: Gagandeep marks his goods 50% above the cost price and offers a discount of 25% on the marked price to his customers. What is the percentage gain of Gagandeep?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price (C.P) = 100 (Assume for simplicity).

Marked price (M.P) = 50% above cost price = 100 + 50% of 100 = 100 + 50 = 150.

Discount = 25% of Marked Price = 25% of 150 = 0.25 × 150 = 37.5.

Selling price (S.P) = Marked price - Discount = 150 - 37.5 = 112.5.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Gain = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Percentage Gain = [(S.P - C.P) / C.P] × 100

⇒ Percentage Gain = [(112.5 - 100) / 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage Gain = [12.5 / 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage Gain = 12.5%

**The percentage gain of Gagandeep is 12.5%.**

questions.question: What will be the average of all the odd numbers from 11 to 71 (both inclusive)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Odd numbers from 11 to 71 (both inclusive).

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all odd numbers) / (Total number of odd numbers).

**Calculation:**

The odd numbers from 11 to 71 are: 11, 13, 15, ..., 71.

These numbers form an arithmetic sequence where:

First term (a) = 11

Last term (l) = 71

Common difference (d) = 2

Number of terms (n):

Using the formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence: aₙ = a + (n-1)d

⇒ 71 = 11 + (n-1) × 2

⇒ 71 - 11 = (n-1) × 2

⇒ 60 = (n-1) × 2

⇒ n-1 = 30

⇒ n = 31

Sum of the sequence (S):

Using the formula for the sum of an arithmetic sequence: S_n = (n)/(2) × (a + l)

⇒ S = (31 / 2) × (11 + 71)

⇒ S = (31 / 2) × 82

⇒ S = 31 × 41

⇒ S = 1271

Average:

Average = Sum / Total number of terms

⇒ Average = 1271 / 31

⇒ Average = 41

**The average of all odd numbers from 11 to 71 is 41.**

⇒ S.I = ₹16,580 × 10 × 4 / 100

⇒ S.I = ₹6632

**Simple Interest on the sum at 10% for 4 years is ₹6,632.**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some rhinos are birds.

All penguins are birds.

Conclusions:

(I): Some rhinos are penguins.

(II): All birds are penguins.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some rhinos are birds.

All penguins are birds.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a65763cd8fc5bbbac2855dd9346e7fd1d669a8f94842d9920da7ad8d20a5570.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43885016d63e45ee84a32875cad4d8ba72d2810d5bde3ee687dfea901997b18a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some rhinos are penguins - **False** (As there is no definite direct relationship given between rhinos and penguins. It is possible that rhinos that are birds are not penguins.)

II. All birds are penguins - **False** (The statement "All penguins are birds" implies that penguins are a subset of birds. It does not imply that all birds are necessarily penguins; there could be other types of birds apart from penguins.)

So, neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows.

questions.question: What do you call the body cavity that is lined by mesoderm?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Coelom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **coelom** is a body cavity that is completely lined by the **mesoderm**, the middle layer of embryonic tissue in triploblastic animals.
 
• This cavity is filled with fluid and provides a space for the development and suspension of internal organs, allowing them to grow and move independently of the body wall.
 
• Coelomates, or animals with a coelom, exhibit a higher level of structural complexity and specialization in organ systems compared to animals without a coelom.
 
• The presence of a coelom is a key characteristic of many higher animal groups, including **annelids, mollusks, arthropods, echinoderms, and chordates**.
 
• The coelom plays an essential role in functions such as **circulation, respiration, and waste elimination** by providing space for the development of complex systems like the digestive and cardiovascular systems.
 
• The coelom also acts as a cushion for internal organs, protecting them from mechanical shocks and injuries.
 
• It allows the body to have a more flexible and efficient movement due to its role in forming a hydrostatic skeleton in some organisms like earthworms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diploblasts**__

 __
 
• **Diploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from two embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm and endoderm**.
 
• They lack a mesoderm, which means they do not develop a true coelom. Examples include **cnidarians** like jellyfish and corals.
 
• These organisms usually have a simple body structure and radial symmetry.
 
 
 
• **Radial Symmetry**__
 __
 
• **Radial symmetry** refers to a body plan in which any plane passing through the central axis divides the organism into identical halves.
 
• This type of symmetry is seen in animals like **cnidarians** (e.g., jellyfish) and **echinoderms** (e.g., starfish in their larval stage).
 
• It is associated with animals that have a sessile or free-floating lifestyle.
 
 
 
• **Triploblasts**__
 
 
• **Triploblastic animals** are organisms that develop from three embryonic germ layers: the **ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm**.
 
• They can be further categorized as **acoelomates (without a coelom), pseudocoelomates, or coelomates** based on the presence and type of coelom.
 
• Examples include most higher animals like **arthropods, mollusks, and vertebrates**.

questions.question:
Meher had two large chunks of coal. She set fire to the first chunk and broke the second one into pieces. Help Meher understand what kind of changes happened to the two chunks of coal at the end of the activity by choosing all the applicable statements.

A. Both chunks of coal underwent physical changes only.

B. The changes were reversible for the first chunk of coal only.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The first chunk of coal was set on fire, which led to a **chemical change**. Burning coal results in the production of heat, light, and gases like carbon dioxide. This is a chemical change because the coal is transformed into new substances, and the change is irreversible.
 
• The second chunk of coal was broken into smaller pieces. Breaking coal into pieces is a **physical change** because it only alters the size or shape of the coal without affecting its chemical composition. This type of change is reversible.
 
• Option **C** correctly identifies that only a **physical change** took place for the second chunk of coal.
 
• Option **E** is accurate in stating that the first case demonstrates a **chemical change**, as burning involves a transformation of substances.
 
• The distinction between physical and chemical changes is important in understanding the properties and behavior of materials under different conditions.

 __
 
• This is incorrect because the first chunk of coal underwent a **chemical change** due to combustion, while only the second chunk experienced a **physical change**.
 
 
 
• **Option B: The changes were reversible for the first chunk of coal only**__
 __
 
• This is inaccurate because the change in the first chunk (burning coal) is irreversible, as it transforms into new substances.
 
 
 
• **Option D: Both chunks of coal underwent chemical changes only**__
